Determines whether a check of the mass-balance over the domain is made or not
sections output file, written by the master
Name of the file into which the C-VSM results of the computation are written, the periodicity being given by the keyword: C-VSM FULL PRINTOUT PERIOD.

Format of the C-VSM RESULT FILE. Possible choices are: SERAFIN : classical single precision format in TELEMAC, SERAFIND: classical double precision format in TELEMAC, MED : MED double precision format based on HDF5.
Name of the file into which 2D time series are written at the points defined in the TIME SERIES COORDINATES FILE.

Format of the TIME SERIES FILE. Possible choices are: SERAFIN : classical single precision format in TELEMAC, SERAFIND: classical double precision format in TELEMAC, MED : MED double precision format based on HDF5.

Previous computation results file format. Possible values are: - SERAFIN : classical single precision format in Telemac; - SERAFIND: classical double precision format in Telemac; - MED : MED format based on HDF5
Wave file format. Possible values are: - SERAFIN : classical single precision format in Telemac; - SERAFIND: classical double precision format in Telemac; - MED : MED format based on HDF5
Name of FORTRAN file to be submitted.
Name of the file containing the types of boundary conditions. This file is filled automatically by the mesh generator through colours that are assigned to the computation domain boundary nodes.

Name of a file containing the results a previous TOMAWAC computation made on the same mesh. The wave data (wave height, wave period, wave angle ) will be given by the last record of the file. The user has to verify that both informations (wave and current data) are consistent. Remark :The wave data can also be specified in the hydrodynamic file. the user has also the possibility to give the values of the wave data in the subroutine USER_FORCING_GAIA. This is recommended for non-steady flow simulation.

Name of the file used to validate the computation. This option is primarily used for the validation documents. The results of the computation will be compared with the values of this file. This file is then considered as a reference which the computation is going to be compared with. The comparison is done by the subroutine BIEF_VALIDA, which can be modified so as to include, for example, a comparison with an exact solution. If present in the steering file, triggers the validation step during the computation since release 9.0 without boolean keyword VALIDATION.
Name of the possible file containing the bathymetric data.
sections input file, partitioned
Name of the file containing points coordinates and periods of time where time series are extracted in the TIME SERIES FILE.

Previous computation results file format. Possible values are: - SERAFIN : classical single precision format in Telemac; - SERAFIND: classical double precision format in Telemac; - MED : MED format based on HDF5

Name of a file containing the results of an earlier sedimentological computation which was made on the same mesh. A recorded time step will provide the initial conditions for the new computation. If present in the steering file, a continuation is done from the result of a previous computation defined by this keyword without boolean keyword COMPUTATION CONTINUED since release 9.0. In that case, all the data from the steering file may be defined once again, which provides an opportunity to change, for example, the time step. It is also possible to define new boundary conditions.
Time in seconds after which bed updates are taken into account
In case of continuation of computation, record number to start from in the PREVIOUS SEDIMENTOLOGICAL COMPUTATION FILE. -1 means the last record is taken.

Name of the file into which the computation results shall be written in order to get a perfect continued computation unlike using the RESULTS FILE. It is then an output file for the current computation, which will be used as an input file when a continued computation is expected to be perfect (the keyword PREVIOUS SEDIMENTOLOGICAL COMPUTATION FILE is then used). The RESTART FILE FORMAT and the PREVIOUS SEDIMENTOLOGICAL COMPUTATION FILE FORMAT have to be set with 'SERAFIND' or 'MED'. If present in the steering file, triggers the writing of this restart file since release 9.0 without boolean keyword RESTART MODE.

Format of the RESTART FILE. Possible choices are: SERAFIN : classical single precision format in TELEMAC, SERAFIND: classical double precision format in TELEMAC, MED : MED double precision format based on HDF5. Only double precision formats ensure a perfect restart.

Determines, in number of time steps, the printout period for the variables to be saved for a perfect restart in the RESTART FILE. Default = 0 means the RESTART FILE is only written at the last time step or at the RECORD NUMBER IN RESTART FILE.

Determines the number of time step when printing the variables to be saved for a perfect restart in the RESTART FILE. Default = -1 means the RESTART FILE is only written at the last time step and/or periodically at the period RESTART FILE PRINTOUT PERIOD.
Names of variables the user wants to write into the graphic results file. Each variable is represented by a letter. See CHOIX1 above. One can use *, *A* means all fractions

choices.QSi: bed load transport rate of sediment of class i

choices.SVYi: sediment i viscosity along y axis (m2/s) - only 3D
choices.SVZi: sediment i viscosity along z axis (m2/s) - only 3D
choices.QSBLX: bed load transport rate x axis
choices.QSBLY: bed load transport rate y axis

keywords.help: Values of prescribed solid discharges at the inflow boundaries (kg/s). One value per liquid boundary
Gives the proportion of the imposed solid discharge for each class. Give one numbre for each non-cohesive class
Sets the initial values of suspended sediment concentration.

Suspended sediment concentration values prescribed at the inflow boundaries. Determines the imposed value of sediments at the first boundary, then at the second and so on, with the same logic as tracers.

Specifies the type of profiles of sediment concentration on the vertical (only for 3D simulations). Possible choices are: 0: user defined, 1: constant, 2: Rouse equilibrium, constant (diluted sediment) or Rouse (sediment), 3: Rouse (normalized) and imposed concentration. 4: Rouse modified with molecular viscosity.

choices.4: 'Modified Rouse profile accounting for molecular viscosity

keywords.keyword: SUSPENDED SEDIMENTS CONCENTRATION VALUES AT THE SOURCES
keywords.help: Values of the suspended sediments at the sources. All sources for the first suspended sediment, then all sources for the second suspended sediment, etc. For example, if there are 3 suspended sediments (SED1, SED2 and SED3) and 2 sources (S1 and S2), the following syntax is used: S1_SED1;S1_SED2;S1_SED3;S2_SED1;S2_SED2;S2_SED3 10.0; 10.0; 0.0; 0.0; 10.0; 10.0

keywords.keyword: SCHEME FOR ADVECTION OF SUSPENDED SEDIMENTS
keywords.help: Choice of the advection scheme for the suspended sediments, ERIA works only in 2D. The order of the chosen scheme must follow the order of the suspended sediments.

keywords.keyword: SCHEME OPTION FOR ADVECTION OF SUSPENDED SEDIMENTS
keywords.help: If N or PSI SCHEME: 1=explicit 2=predictor-corrector 3= predictor-corrector second-order in time 4= implicit

keywords.keyword: SCHEME FOR DIFFUSION OF SUSPENDED SEDIMENTS IN 3D
keywords.help: Monitors the choice of the diffusion scheme for sediments in 3D simulations. Possible choices are: 0: no diffusion, 1: implicit.

Choice of the solver for suspension resolution. Possible choices are: 1: conjugate gradient, 2: conjugate residual, 3: conjugate gradient on a normal equation, 4: minimum error, 5: squared conjugate gradient, 6: CGSTAB, 7: GMRES, 8: direct solver.

choices.3: conjugate gradient on a normal equation

keywords.keyword: SOLVER OPTION FOR DIFFUSION OF SUSPENSION
keywords.help: Dimension of Krylov space for the GMRES method (7).

keywords.keyword: MAXIMUM NUMBER OF ITERATIONS FOR SOLVER FOR SUSPENSION
keywords.help: Limits the number of solver iterations for the diffusion of sediments.
Sets the accuracy needed for the computation of the diffusion of suspension. It is not possible to set different values for different solvers, only one is accepted.

Choice of preconditioning for the diffusion of sediments. Possible choices are: 0: no preconditioning, 2: diagonal, 3: diagonal with the condensed matrix in 3D, 5: diagonal with absolute values in 3D, 7: Crout, 11: Gauss-Seidel EBE in 3D, 13: matrix defined by the user in 3D, 14: diagonal and Crout, 17: direct solver on the vertical in 3D, 21: diagonal condensed and Crout in 3D, 34: diagonal and direct solver on the vertical in 3D.

choices.34: diagonal and direct solver on the vertical

keywords.keyword: FINITE VOLUME SCHEME FOR SUSPENDED SEDIMENTS DIFFUSION
keywords.help: Choice of the finite volume diffusion model: 1: explicit P1 finite element, 2: two points flux, 3: reconstructed two points flux.
Choice of the vertical scheme for diffusion and settling of sediment (only in 3D): 0: Implicit-diffusion scheme, 1: Implicit-convection scheme (Tridiagonal matrix solver), 2: set_fall.f
Decides if hindered formulation is to be used to compute settling velocity for mud.
Type of hindered settling: 0 : User defined formula 1 : Whitehouse et al. (2000) 2 : Winterwerp (1999)
The sediment concentration at which sediment forms a weak soil in kg/m^3. These values are needed when HINDERED SETTLING = YES.
The sediment concentration at which hindered settling is initiated. These values are needed when HINDERED SETTLING = YES.
Decides if hindered formulation is to be used to compute settling velocity for mud. Only in 3D.
Type of flocculation formula: 0: User defined formula ; 1: Van Leussen ; 2: Soulsby et al. (2013).

When the influence of turbulence on the settling velocity is modelled, this coefficient traduces the formation of flocs by turbulence (coefficient a of Van Leussen formula). Value to be imposed if INFLUENCE OF TURBULENCE ON SETTLING VELOCITY = YES.

When the influence of turbulence on the settling velocity is modelled, this coefficient traduces the breaking of flocs by turbulence (coefficient b of Van Leussen formula). Value to be imposed if INFLUENCE OF TURBULENCE ON SETTLING VELOCITY = YES.
Sets the zero of GAIA used for clipping values.
Set finite volumes method or not
Possible choices are: 1: classic, 2: frontal. Beware, with option 2, a special numbering of points is required.
Defines the method to store matrices. The possible choices are: 1: classical EBE, 3: edge-based storage.
Parameter for FV solving the Exner equation, 0.5 = Centered (precise), 1 = Upwind (stable because diffusive)

keywords.keyword: MAXIMUM NUMBER OF ITERATIONS FOR POSITIVE THICKNESS
keywords.help: Only for bedload in finite elements. Parameter for positive_depths. Old default value = 10 until release 8.1.
1: Flat bed, 2: Rippled bed, 3: Dunes and mega ripples (Method of Van Rijn)
Defines the number of user derivatives, within the framework of the algorithmic differentiation.
Name of user derivatives in 32 characters, 16 for the name, 16 for the unit.
Defines the number of directions for the differentiators
Enables the symbolic linear solver for AD.
Resets the derivatives for AD.
Iterative linear solvers: derivative convergence test for AD.
Sets the value of the sediment density for each class en Kg/m3
The bed volume concentration CSF=(1-porosity) is used to calculate the bed evolution of non-cohesive sand transport.
Specifies the water kinematic viscosity. M/S2
Uses the velocity profile based on the Miles approximation
Sets the value of settling velocity for every sediment. Give a negative value to use the Stokes, Zanke or Van Rijn formulae (depending on the grain size)
Activate suspension for all the sands in the simulation. It is not possible to have a different behaviour between sand classes. Mud is always considered in suspension.

Imposes the equilibrium concentration at the inlet boundaries in 2D cases. For non cohesive sediments, the equilibrium near bed concentration is computed with respect to the suspension transport formula for all sands.

keywords.keyword: SUSPENSION TRANSPORT FORMULA FOR ALL SANDS
keywords.help: Different choice to compute the equilibrium near-bed concentration 1 : Zysderman and Fredsoe, equilibrium formula 2: Bijker method. The near bed concentration is related to the bedload . This option cannot be used without bedload transport 3: Van Rijn formula 4: Soulsby_van Rijn formula
Modification of 2D convection velocities to account for velocity and concentration profiles

keywords.keyword: CLASSES CRITICAL SHEAR STRESS FOR MUD DEPOSITION
keywords.help: Critical shear stress for deposition (Pa)
constant of the Krone and Partheniades erosion law (Kg/m2/s)

keywords.keyword: COEFFICIENT FOR DIFFUSION OF SUSPENDED SEDIMENTS
keywords.help: Sets the value of the suspended sediments diffusivity in 2D. This value may have a significant effect on the evolution of sediments in time. It is a scalar (one value for all sediments).

keywords.keyword: COEFFICIENT FOR HORIZONTAL DIFFUSION OF SUSPENDED SEDIMENTS
keywords.help: Sets the values of the horizontal diffusion of sediments in 3D. These values may have a significant effect on the evolution of sediments in time. It is an array, with one value per suspended sediment, separated by semicolons.

keywords.keyword: COEFFICIENT FOR VERTICAL DIFFUSION OF SUSPENDED SEDIMENTS
keywords.help: Sets the values of the vertical diffusion of sediments in 3D. These values may have a significant effect on the evolution of sediments in time. It is an array, with one value per suspended sediment, separated by semicolons.
Sets value of diameter dm for particular size class.
Sets value of hiding factor for particular size class.
Sets the value of the initial fraction of each sediment class. Beware that the sum over all classes must be equal to 1.
Thickness for bed stratification. Composition of first layer is used to compute bed load transport rate. If you do not want a stratification, use a large value
4 hiding factor formulas are implemented in GAIA 0: const => need to give CLASSES HIDING FACTOR 1: Egiazaroff 2: Ashida & Michiue : 4: Karim, Holly & Yang
constant active layer thickness or not
Sediment layers thickness (m) for initialisation.

keywords.keyword: D90 SAND DIAMETER FOR ONLY ONE CLASS
keywords.help: Sets the value of diameter d90 for simulations with one sand class. With multiple sand classes, D90 is computed by GAIA.

keywords.keyword: RATIO BETWEEN SKIN FRICTION AND MEAN DIAMETER
keywords.help: Ratio for the computation of skin friction. skin roughness = ratio * mean diameter (for the mixture of sand, the mean diameter used is a value per node which is computed thanks to the fraction and the mean diameter of each sediment for each node of the mesh) if KSPRATIO =0 : use skin friction prediction from Van Rijn (2007) for currents and the Wiberg and Harris method for waves

Formula to modify the shear stress in sediment flow rate formulae so they use the skin bed roughness (see also KSPRATIO) 0 : No correction (TAUP= TOB), valid if the roughness provided to TELEMAC is physical - close to the skin roughness, usually estimated to 3d50 1 : Correction for a flat bed (KSP= KSPRATIO * D50) 2 : Ripple correction factor

Possible choices: 1: formula of Koch et Flokstra, modification of bed load linked keyword : BETA. 2 : formula of Soulsby, modification critical shear stress, can only be used with a threshold fomula. Linked keyword : FRICTION ANGLE OF THE SEDIMENT 3 : formula of Apsley and Stansby, modification of critical shear stress and the bed load. Linked keyword: FRICTION ANGLE OF THE SEDIMENT 4 : formula of Apsley and Stansby, modification of critical shear stress and the bed load and additionally avalanching. Linked keyword: ANGLE DE FROTTEMENT DU SEDIMENT
Angle of repose of the sediment. Used in the Soulsby formula to take into account the influence of bed slope on critical shear stress. Use if ...=2
1: Koch and Flokstra 2: formula of Talmon et al. 1995, JHR 33(4) formulas (1) and (17) linked keyword : BETA2
Parameter pour la deviation pour la formule de Talmon et al.
Two choices of formulas, both take FRICTION ANGLE OF THE SEDIMENT into account: 0: No sliding 1: Sliding classic 2: Avalanching according Apsley and Stansby
If yes, slope effect taken into account: deviation + modification of critical shear stress. NO will cancel the key-words FORMULA FOR SLOPE EFFECT and FORMULA FOR DEVIATION
Specifies the value of the beta coefficient used in the Koch and Flokstra slope effect formulation.

keywords.keyword: COMPUTE BED ROUGHNESS AT SEDIMENT SCALE
keywords.help: Compute a bed roughness at the sediment scale - see BED ROUGHNESS PREDICTOR OPTION -. It can be different from the hydrodynamics roughness due to the action of waves or to a space-time varying grain size distribution. This roughness could be sent to Telemac but it is not supported yet.
Alpha coefficient of secondary current(-), Should be chosen between 0.75 (rough bottom) and 1 (smooth bottom)
Amplification coefficient for bed evolution

keywords.keyword: OUTPUT TIME ACCORDING TO MORPHOLOGICAL FACTOR
keywords.help: If yes the output time in the GAIA result file will be equal to the hydrodynamic time multiplied by the morphological factor.
To cancel sediment fluxes to and from dry points
Enables bedload for all sands

keywords.keyword: BED-LOAD TRANSPORT FORMULA FOR ALL SANDS
keywords.help: 10 bed-load or total load transport formulas are implemented in GAIA. The formula Ne3, Ne30 and Ne9 should not be used in the case of coupling with the suspension. The formula Ne4, Ne5, Ne8 and Ne9 model the transport under the combined action of currents and waves : 1 : MEYER-PETER (bed load) 2 : EINSTEIN-BROWN (bed load) 3 : ENGELUND-HANSEN + CHOLLET AND CUNGE (VERSION 5.3) 30: ENGELUND-HANSEN (total) 4 : BIJKER (bed load + suspension) 5 : SOULSBY - VAN RIJN (bed load + suspension) 6 : HUNZIKER (only for sand grading) IN THIS CASE HIDING FACTOR KEYWORD DISCARDED And Hunziker formula used 7 : VAN RIJN (bed load) 8 : BAILARD (bed load + suspension) 9 : DIBAJNIA ET WATANABE (total) 10 : WILCOCK AND CROWE (graded sediment) Users can also program other formulas (subroutine bedload_qb_user.f) setting this key word to zero : 0 : FORMULA PROGRAMMED BY USER Warning : it is not then possible to choose the option VARIABLE TIME-STEP

keywords.keyword: B VALUE FOR THE BIJKER FORMULA
keywords.help: b value for the Bijker formula
Alpha coefficient for Meyer-Peter and Muller formula
3 kinds of bed model are available: 1 : multilayers (automatic active layer if several classes) 2 : multilayer with consolidation 3 : consolidation model based on Gibson theory
Liste of types of sediment: cohesive (CO) ou non cohesive (NCO).

keywords.keyword: NUMBER OF LAYERS OF THE CONSOLIDATION MODEL
keywords.help: Vertical bed structure - The number of layers should be less than 10
Mass transfert coefficients of the multilayer consolidation model in s-1
Concentrations of the mud-bed in g per l (per layer)

keywords.keyword: LAYERS CRITICAL EROSION SHEAR STRESS OF THE MUD
keywords.help: Critical erosion shear stress of the mud per layer (N per m2)
Defines the model of the vertical grain sorting: 0 = HR-VSM = Layer Model (Classic Hirano / Ribberink approach) 1 = C-VSM (Continous Vertical Grain Sorting Model)

Defines the maximum discretisation of the Continous Vertical Sorting Model: Should be bigger than 8xNumber of Fractions. The bigger the higher the RAM requirements, but the faster and accurater the bookkeeping of the sediments.
Number of Timesteps to next printout of the full C-VSM. These printouts are highly time and disc consuming. 0 = Coupled to GRAPHIC PRINTOUT PERIOD >0 = Own printout period for the C-VSM

Printout the C-VSM for the whole model as 3D C-VSM RESULTS FILE or / and for some nodes as C-VSM NODE FILE Give Up to 100 INTEGER numbers separated by ';' 0 = Full model .-> VSPRES N = 1,2...NPOINT; 2D-ID of a SELFIN MESH POINT ->*_VSP.CSV

MODEL FOR ACTIVE LAYER THICKNESS 0 = ELAY0 (Keyword: ACTIVE LAYER THICKNESS) 1 = Hunziker & Gunther 2 = Fredsoe & Deigaard (1992) 3 = van RIJN (1993) 4 = Wong (2006) 5 = Malcherek (2003) 6 = 3*d50 within last time steps ALT
